summary: Two Utah men in an experimental AutoGyro Calidus gyroplane crashed in a remote canyon about 12 miles southeast of the Glade Park Fire Station after a downdraft left them unable to climb out; pilot Mike Burton, 53, of Pleasant Grove UT and passenger Josh Humphries, 30, of Payson UT survived with back and neck injuries. CareFlight located the site with night-vision equipment but could not land in the heavy snow; a snowmobile ground rescue reached the pair around 8:20 p.m. Burton was flown to a Grand Junction hospital, Humphries was snowmobiled to a waiting ambulance.
responding_agency: Mesa County Search and Rescue; Mesa County Sheriff's Office; Glade Park Fire Department; Grand Junction Fire Department; CareFlight; Delta County Dispatch
notes: Incident-focused: victim roles stated as pilot/passenger only, no other personal detail. NBC11 story via Kathryn's Report 05/20/16 archive (parent-opened 2026-09-17): crash 'Tuesday night' 2016-05-17 (Tuesday-verified; Monday 5/16 demo trip to Telluride, Wednesday 5/18 return). Burton built the Calidus himself through Air-Gyro Aviation. The same archive page's N50NE NTSB entries are distinct incidents: 2015-01-06 Johnson Creek south of Glade Park CO (no SAR-response detail, not inserted) and 2016-05-20 Fruitland UT (out of scope).
